To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DMI, CIT, MIA, retinoic acid and phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate increase the transcriptional activity from the D2 receptor gene in the Neuro 2A cells, (2) DMI, but not CIT or MIA, increases the transcriptional activity in SH-SY5 cells, (3) in the Neuro 4A cells, the increase in transcriptional activation by ADs is mediated by protein kinase A
the transcriptional activity in the dopamine D2 gene promoter in the Neuro 2A cells was significantly increased after 24-72 h incubation with DMI, CIT or MIA.

the three antidepressant drugs, desipramine, citalopram and mianserin, increased the transcriptional activity in the dopamine D2 promoter in three different neuroblastoma cell line, Neuro 2A, SH-SY 5Y and NB 41A3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in vitro model for studying the effect of ADs on transcription of the dopamine D1 and D2 receptor genes.
the possibility of using the neuronal cell lines transfected by the dopamine D2 promoter to model the effect of ADs on the transcription of the dopamine D(2) receptor gene.
the development of a new model for studying the molecular mechanisms of action of antidepressant drugs, and the results obtained may be useful for the development of new antidepressants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the studied ADs increase transcriptional activity of human dopamine D2 receptor promoter in a cell-type specific manner and that this effect is mediated, at least in part, by the protein kinase A pathway.
the ADs, DMI, CIT, and MIA, at doses of 0,1-1 micro M for 24 h, increase the transcriptional activity in the dopamine D2 promoter in the Neuro 2A and SH-SY5y cell line.

the transcription of dopamine D2 receptors in neuroblastoma cells is increased in a dose-dependent manner by the antidepressants, desipramine, citalopram and mianserin, and this effect is mediated through the protein kinase A-dependent mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptional activity in the dopamine D2 promoter can be regulated by a variety of compounds, including retinoic acid and ADs.
the transcriptional activity is increased by ADs, retinoic acid and forskolin, as well as protein kinase A and protein kinase C pathways.
DMI and CIT increase the transcriptional activity via the activation of protein kinase A and protein kinase C pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dopamine D2 gene promoter can be used as a model for investigating the effects of ADs on transcriptional activity of a specific gene in neuronal cells.
the neuroblastoma cells transfected with the D2R promoter can be used as a model system to study the effects of ADs on the transcriptional regulation of the D2R gene.
ADs, which are used to treat depression, increase the transcriptional activity dopamine D2 receptor promoter in the neuronal cell lines.
